summary: Alexander’s Macedonian monarchy conquered the Achaemenid realm, linking Greece, Egypt and western Asia before fragmenting after his death.
currency: Silver drachm-based coinage, including tetradrachms issued in Alexander’s name.
military: Campaigns from 334 to 323 BCE carried Macedonian armies through the Persian Empire to northwestern South Asia.
contributions: Conquest accelerated exchanges between Greek and other cultures that shaped the subsequent Hellenistic kingdoms.
origin: Alexander inherited Macedonia’s throne in 336 BCE and launched the invasion of Persian territory in 334 BCE.
decline: After Alexander died in 323 BCE, rival generals fought over and divided his territories.
periodNote: Dates describe Alexander’s reign; the Asian conquests began in 334 BCE, and successor governments persisted after his death.
